# XER Schedule Check: DCMA 14-point assessment of a Primavera P6 XER file

> Free, in-browser DCMA 14-point schedule check for Primavera P6 .xer exports. It reads the XER tables, recomputes early and late dates and total float on each activity's own calendar with P6's relationship, lag-calendar, constraint and progress rules (equal to P6's stored values on 18,133 of 19,822 open activities in six public files from P6 5.0 to 24.12), runs the 14 points with the DCMA thresholds and a 600-day critical path test, and lists every activity behind each finding, plus logic loops, out-of-sequence progress and open finishes. Nothing is uploaded.

Free and open source (MIT). Screening metrics on the user's own file, not scheduling, contractual or legal advice. Missed tasks and BEI use P6's planned dates as the baseline because a single XER rarely carries the baseline project. Not modelled: resource levelling, expected finish dates, part of P6's retained-logic rule for started activities with mixed FS and SS predecessors. Not affiliated with Oracle, Primavera or the DCMA.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/xer-schedule-check/)

## For agents

- Engine: `xer.mjs` `parseXer(decodeXer(bytes))`; `cpm.mjs` `schedule(xer)` (dates in wall-clock minutes, float in hours) and `drivingPath(result, projId)`; `dcma.mjs` `assess(xer, { projId })` returns `{ project, checks[14], extra, recompute, drivingPath }` and `findingsCsv(report)`.
- CLI: `node cli.mjs schedule.xer [--json] [--csv out.csv] [--project CODE]`.

- [Source code and README](https://github.com/duncan-haywood/oss-monorepo/tree/main/ventures/xer-schedule-check): MIT licensed. Measurements: `eval/cpm-vs-p6-2026-11-19.md`.
